Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  February 5, 2026
The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on February 5, 2026. Commissioner
Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:06 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Christopher
  Beck - District 4, Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at
  Large
  Absent:  Commissioner Octavio Padilla - District 2, Vacant - District 3

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director of Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Teresa Estrada  Assistant Director
  Baz Devlia  Human Services Superintendent
  Brian McClure  Parks Administration Superintendent
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Program Specialist

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Beck and seconded by Commissioner Brown
that the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on November 6,
2025, be approved. The following roll call vote carried the motion:
Ayes: Commissioner Brown, Beck, and Denmon
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Parks Administration Superintendent Brian McClure
reported the following: Parks Division - Park staff replanted the center median on
Manchester Boulevard near the 405 freeway for quarterly maintenance. The Planning
Commission approved the development of a community garden at the vacant lot adjacent
to Siminski Park. On Sunday, February 15th, the NBA will be hosting a “Total Health Walk”
at Edward Vincent Park and will be using the basketball courts for All-star Weekend.
Graffiti Division - The Graffiti Division purchased a new pressure washer last year and we
are systematically removing all paint from the bottom of the light poles as opposed to
painting over the graffiti. The Graffiti hotline is (310) 412-8739. Tree Division - on Monday,
February 9th, a major tree removal will take place at Edward Vincent Park. West Coast

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

Arborists will be removing all the trees underneath the Southern California Edison utility
lines.

REPORT - RECREATION. Assistant Director Teresa Estrada reported the following: Youth
Sports Event - The new sports event year is here, marking the start of the winter season
of citywide sports in Inglewood. The Inglewood Youth Sports League is proud to offer
basketball and soccer leagues this winter. Our Inglewood Jr. Clippers basketball league is
currently holding weekly practices, with volunteer coaches working to build team
chemistry with their players. Each team is permitted (1) practice per week, lasting one -
hour, at either Darby or Rogers Park. Basketball remains popular in Inglewood, as
evidenced by over 350 participants, 28 teams, and 7 divisions serving youth ages 4 to 14.
The league includes 82 female participants competing in the Tiny Might (Ages 5-8) and
Mighty Might (Ages 9-13) divisions. All Inglewood Youth Sports Leagues emphasize
learning the game, fundamental development, and enjoying the competition. Basketball
games will start the first week of February and will end with Championship on Saturday
April 11TH. The winter season also brings our fastest-growing Inglewood Youth Soccer
League sports program. The soccer league started in winter 2024 with 57 participants. This
year, the league has grown to 217 participants with a 50-person waiting list. The league
has expanded so quickly that we cannot currently accommodate more players without
willing volunteer coaches. It serves young people ages 4-12 with 20 teams across four
different age divisions. The teams are coed, with 50 female participants. With practices
just beginning, teams are focused on mastering fundamentals, getting in shape, and
learning the rules. The league’s practices and games are held at the beautiful, newly
resurfaced Champions Field at Edward Vincent Jr. Park. Games are on Saturdays from 9:00
am to 2:00 pm. The season runs from February 7th through April 11th. Come out and watch
the basketball and soccer action in support of our Inglewood youth on Thursday nights and
all day on Saturdays. You won’t be disappointed, as the action is cute, fast, fun, and
unpredictable. Black History Celebration - The City’s 4th annual Black History Celebration
will be held on Saturday, February 21st, in downtown Inglewood along Market Street, from
11:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The event will include a lively lineup of live entertainment, art
displays, health screenings, and a variety of informational, commercial, and food vendors.
A key feature of the celebration will be the Black History Speech Contest, where selected
winners will deliver powerful and inspiring speeches. I encourage everyone to join us for
this special occasion. Black History Art Exhibit - I invite everyone to join the Parks and
Recreation department for a special art exhibit on Saturday, February 28, from 12:00 to
4:00 p.m. at Darby Park. Titled “Inglewood Through the Eras: Black Excellence in Public
Life,” this exhibit will tell the city's story and highlight Black leaders and community
members whose service, leadership, and excellence have helped shape Inglewood across
generations. We welcome you to this meaningful and inspiring event.

   Park and Recreation Commission

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Superintendent Baz Devlia reported on the
following: Senior Nutrition Programs - We are serving approximately 430 seniors per day
through home-delivered meals for homebound seniors and congregate meals. Fresh
produce is offered weekly in partnership with the Social Justice Learning Institute, along
with monthly shelf-stable meal boxes in collaboration with the Los Angeles Food
Bank. Nutrition has just completed the disbursement of Emergency Meals. June will bring
Farmers' Market card distribution, and seniors have been able to take several trips to the
market from the center through our transportation services. In the month of February, we
will have special meals for Valentine's Day, Ash Wednesday, and Black History Month.
Senior Center Paratransit - The paratransit program continues to provide trips to seniors
and the disabled community in Inglewood and Hawthorne. The Senior Center recently
hosted a Metro Transportation Pop-Up that promoted their “On the Move Program” for
seniors as well as shared information about another Metro service called Metro Micro.
Metro’s STAR program was also onsite to provide those in mobility devices, free marking
and tethering services, making riding transportation faster and safer for all. Overall, the
pop up brought awareness to the various transportation resources that are available to
seniors and the disabled communities in our city. Another transportation service provider
that participated was “Butterflies,” who partners with the LA Urban League, and is also
geared towards those using assistive and mobility devices who need transportation
services. Transportation services will be closed for the city’s upcoming holiday observance
of Presidents’ Day, which is on Monday, February, 16, 2026. Those that are interested in
booking for the day after the holiday should book no later than Friday, February 13, to
ensure their trips are reserved for Tuesday, February 17, 2026. Senior Center Activities,
Classes, and Trips - Our Senior Center continues to grow, with a diverse range of exciting
presentations and activities planned for this month. On February 6, Alzheimer’s Los
Angeles will be conducting a presentation on “Holding the Pieces”. On February 12, we will
be showing the movie “Pride & Prejudice”. On February 18, we will have a special program
in honor of Black History Month (Poetry Reading, Spoken Words from our seniors) from
10:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. On February 23, Los Angeles County Department of Mental Health
will be conducting a presentation on “Stress Management”. On February 25TH, we will be
having our monthly dance from 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department Director
Thomas Uwal reported on the following: Edward Vincent Park Tennis Court
Encroachments - Southern California Edison (SCE) has conducted an evaluation of the
encroachment area located between Florence Avenue and the Edward Vincent Park tennis
courts. SCE determined that all trees within this area must be removed due to fire hazard
concerns and the need for unobstructed access to the site. The Parks, Recreation and
Community Services Department continues to collaborate with the Public Works
Department and Southern California Edison to identify solutions that will provide SCE with
safe and efficient access to the location. At this time, staff is reviewing and assessing the

costs associated with the removal of the affected trees. Blue Zones Mayor’s Initiative (Fall
Risk Prevention Program) - the Blue Zones program focuses on strategies that promote
longevity, high vitality, reduced disease rates, and strong cognitive health, commonly
supporting individuals who live to age 100 and beyond. The program emphasizes the
“Power 9” lifestyle principles, which include plant-based nutrition, natural daily
movement, strong social connections, sense of purpose, and stress reduction. Through a
mayoral initiative, the City of Inglewood is implementing a Blue Zones–inspired program
with a specific emphasis on fall risk prevention for seniors. This class is designed to
significantly reduce fall-related risks among older adults. The exercise program will be
carefully tailored for seniors with medical conditions such as arthritis, osteoporosis,
cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and balance disorders. To support the program’s
development, professional organizations with credentials are working on a curriculum
vitae with individuals that holds a Doctorate in Physical Therapy. There has been strong
enthusiasm from senior participants, and the program is anticipated to begin in mid-
February. FIFA World Cup Community Events - The City is assisting Trifiletti Consulting
with plans to host two community events on Market Street in conjunction with the FIFA
World Cup. The proposed event dates are Friday, June 12, 2026, and Friday, July 10,
2026.These events aim to engage the community by celebrating the World Cup in
Inglewood and are expected to include vendors, soccer clinics, food, and family-friendly
activities. Attendance is anticipated to be comparable to participation levels seen during
Black History Month and Hispanic Heritage celebrations. Recognition of Ms. Maxine Toller
- Ms. Maxine Toller, a longtime participant of the Inglewood Senior Center, passed away
during the first week of January. She dedicated her life to serving the senior community
and demonstrated unwavering commitment as a board member of the Inglewood Senior
Center Advisory Committee. In recognition of her service and lasting impact, it is
respectfully requested that the Parks, Recreation and Community Services Commission
close its meeting in her honor. The Mayor and City Council closed its meeting in her honor
two weeks ago and gave her family a commendation for being a true public servant in the
City of Inglewood.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. Mrs. Brown commended staff for the City being clean.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Beck dittoed sentiments with praise, a
“testament to leadership”. Commissioner Brown addressed heavy traffic concerns and
suggested having officers regulate the traffic during large events held in the City.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:56 p.m.
